targets.name: Jezero Crater

location.note: Window centred on the Mars 2020 landing site region, crater floor and delta.

methodology.aridity: PROXY. P/PET -> 0: Mars has no liquid precipitation (P = 0) while evaporative demand is non-zero, so the aridity index is 0 by construction (hyper-arid limit).
methodology.annual_temperature_range: Max minus min over 12 Ls bins (30 deg) of the diurnal-mean air temperature from MEDA ATS (median of the three RSM sensors, ~1.45 m), 335 sols of one Mars year. Bin means 212.61..223.93 K. A Mars 'month' (30 deg Ls) lasts ~56 sols vs ~30 days on Earth.
methodology.elevation: PROXY. Absolute elevations on different bodies are referenced to unrelated datums and are not physically comparable. The criterion is therefore re-interpreted as 'thin atmosphere': Earth pressure falls with altitude, and no Earth surface reaches Mars or Moon surface pressure, so the target is set to the highest mean elevation of any valid Earth cell (5702.0 m). Similarity on this criterion therefore rewards the lowest-pressure Earth terrain available. MEDA median surface pressure at Jezero ~740 Pa (Earth sea level ~101 325 Pa). Raw MOLA mean elevation of the window -2310 m (areoid) is reported, not used.
methodology.slope: Horn (1981) slope on a 926.6 m grid binned from MGS MOLA 463 m DEM, mean over a 55.6 km x 55.6 km window -- the same code path as Earth.
methodology.surface_roughness: Std. dev. of 926.6 m-binned MOLA elevations in the same window.
methodology.lst_diurnal_range: MEDA TIRS ground temperature, mean over 12 Ls bins of T(13-14 LTST) - T(01-02 LTST): the MODIS Aqua overpass local times.

sources: NASA PDS Atmospheres Node - Mars 2020 MEDA calibrated environment data (urn:nasa:pds:mars2020_meda)
USGS Astrogeology / NASA PDS - MGS MOLA DEM mosaic 463 m
Rodriguez-Manfredi et al. (2021) Space Sci. Rev. 217:48, MEDA instrument description
limitations: Rover-scale (metres) MEDA point measurements are compared with 55 km Earth cell means.
Mars gravity (0.38 g), CO2 atmosphere at ~0.6-0.9 kPa and radiation are not modelled.
Sol-sampling of MEDA is uneven across Ls; each Ls bin is weighted equally.
The MOLA 463 m DEM under-samples metre-scale rover hazards.

proxy_method.aridity: definition: P = 0 on a body without liquid precipitation => P/PET = 0 (hyper-arid limit)
proxy_method.elevation: thin-atmosphere reinterpretation: target = maximum mean elevation of valid Earth cells; rewards the lowest-pressure Earth terrain. NOT a comparison of planetary elevations.

targets.interpretation: Similarity to this target means similar values of the selected modelled variables under the chosen weights. It is not physical, geological or engineering equivalence.

targets.name: Lunar South Pole

location.note: 55.6 km window centred on the pole; includes Shackleton crater and adjacent ridges considered for Artemis landing regions.

methodology.aridity: PROXY. No atmosphere and no precipitation: aridity index 0 by construction.
methodology.annual_temperature_range: NOT APPLICABLE. The Moon has no near-surface air; this criterion is excluded from every lunar score (null, never filled).
methodology.elevation: PROXY. Absolute elevations on different bodies are referenced to unrelated datums and are not physically comparable. The criterion is therefore re-interpreted as 'thin atmosphere': Earth pressure falls with altitude, and no Earth surface reaches Mars or Moon surface pressure, so the target is set to the highest mean elevation of any valid Earth cell (5702.0 m). Similarity on this criterion therefore rewards the lowest-pressure Earth terrain available. The Moon has an exosphere only (surface pressure ~0).
methodology.slope: Horn (1981) slope on a 926.6 m grid binned from LRO LOLA 118 m LDEM, mean over a 55.6 km window centred on the pole -- same code path as Earth.
methodology.surface_roughness: Std. dev. of 926.6 m-binned LOLA elevations in the same window.
methodology.lst_diurnal_range: Diviner polar hourly bolometric temperature maps (Williams et al. 2019): window mean of T(13-14 h local time) - T(01-02 h), averaged over the summer and winter maps. Bin check: the summer hour14 map equals the mean of the PDS 0.25-h products LTIM53-56 (13.00-14.00 h) to 7e-6 K rms (verified, docs/SCIENTIFIC_AUDIT.md); hour02 follows the same numbering (not separately checked). At the pole 'local time' is solar azimuth; slopes facing away from the Sun give negative differences (p10 summer -21.4 K, p90 172.2 K).

sources: NASA PDS / USGS Astrogeology - LRO LOLA global LDEM 118 m (Mar 2014)
LRO Diviner polar hourly temperature maps - Williams et al. (2019) JGR Planets 124:2505
UCLA Diviner level-4 polar products (PDS-archived counterparts)
limitations: Vacuum, 0.17 g, 29.5-day lunation and extreme illumination geometry are not modelled.
Diviner bolometric brightness temperature vs MODIS split-window LST: related but not identical retrievals.
Permanently shadowed and sunlit terrain are averaged together in one 55.6 km window.
